what_its_for: Tofacitinib is used to treat certain conditions where your immune system is overactive and causes inflammation. These include rheumatoid arthritis (joint pain and swelling), psoriatic arthritis (joint pain related to a skin condition), ulcerative colitis (a bowel disease causing stomach pain and diarrhea), and ankylosing spondylitis (spine inflammation). It works by blocking certain proteins in your body called JAK enzymes that trigger inflammation.
how_to_take: Take tofacitinib exactly as your doctor prescribes. You can take it with or without food. Swallow the extended-release tablet (Xeljanz XR) whole — do not crush, split, or chew it. The regular tablet (Xeljanz) can be taken as directed, usually twice a day. Take it at the same time(s) each day to help you remember.
dosing: The usual doses are: Rheumatoid Arthritis or Psoriatic Arthritis — 5 mg twice daily (regular tablet) or 11 mg once daily (extended-release). Ulcerative Colitis — starting dose is 10 mg twice daily for the first 8 weeks, then reduced to 5 mg twice daily for maintenance. Ankylosing Spondylitis — 5 mg twice daily or 11 mg once daily (extended-release). Your doctor may adjust your dose based on your response and any side effects. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is not too close to your next scheduled dose. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store tofacitinib at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Store it in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medications safely out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medication down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid contact with people who are sick or have infections, as tofacitinib weakens your immune system and makes it harder to fight illness. Do not receive live vaccines (such as the nasal flu spray, shingles live vaccine, or yellow fever vaccine) while taking this medicine — talk to your doctor about safe vaccines. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice, as it may affect how the medicine works in your body. Limit alcohol, as it may increase the risk of certain side effects. Do not start tofacitinib if you have an active infection.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience any of the following: signs of infection such as fever, chills, sweating, cough, or painful urination; unusual tiredness or weakness; shortness of breath or chest pain; signs of a blood clot such as leg pain, swelling, or sudden severe headache; stomach pain, bloody or black stools; skin changes or new lumps; yellowing of the skin or eyes (signs of liver problems); or any new or worsening symptoms. Tofacitinib may increase the risk of serious infections, certain cancers, heart problems, and blood clots — your doctor will monitor you regularly with blood tests.
when_it_works: You may begin to notice some improvement in symptoms such as joint pain and swelling within 2 to 4 weeks. However, it may take 3 to 6 months of regular use to experience the full benefit of this medication. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor, even if you feel better.
special_populations: Older adults (age 65 and over): Use with extra caution as the risk of serious infections, heart problems, and certain cancers may be higher. Your doctor will monitor you closely. Pregnancy: Tofacitinib is not recommended during pregnancy as it may harm an unborn baby. Use effective birth control while taking it and for at least 4 weeks after stopping. Tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine, as it may pass into breast milk and harm the baby. Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose if you have reduced kidney or liver function. Children: Safety and dosing in children have not been fully established for all conditions — ask your doctor.
